subject: ventures/solar-panel-cleaning-quote-planner
professional: an owner-operator of a solar panel and window cleaning business who prices jobs weekly (first check: does the quote cover crew time, travel and a minimum call-out, and are the speed and access factors defensible); with a solar performance engineer for the customer-payback side (first check: is the soiling-loss assumption realistic)

evidence.correctness: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the venture dir: 24 pass, 0 fail. Recomputed by hand and compared with calc.mjs output: (1) 20 panels ground, 2 min/panel, setup 10, travel 20, $30/h, 10 km at $0.50, $5 consumables, 40% margin: wall 70 min, labour 35, vehicle 5, total 45, price 45/0.6 = 75.00; code gives 70 / 45 / 75. (2) 14 panels two-storey (x1.9), crew 2, 10% overhead, travel 15 min and 9 km: panel time 53.2/2 = 26.6, wall 51.6, labour 51.6/60*30*2 = 51.6, overhead 5.16, vehicle 4.5, consumables 5, total 66.26, price 110.433; code gives 51.6 / 66.26 / 110.433. (3) Payback 6 kW x 1300 kWh/kW = 7800 kWh, 5% loss = 390 kWh x $0.20 = $78 against a $100 clean = net -$22, break-even loss 100/(7800*0.2) = 6.41%; code gives the same. Also first-fit-decreasing packing checked on 4 identical 48-minute jobs in a 3-hour day: 3 in day one (144 min), 1 in day two, as expected. Hand arithmetic only, no external tool or published tariff compared, so correctness stays at 3 (the arithmetic is right; the inputs are the user's).
evidence.completeness: Features claimed in README/VENTURE.yaml and checked in calc.mjs and index.html: per-job quote at target margin (works), price-per-panel curve (works, tested), day pack (works, tested incl. over-length job flag), annual plan (works), customer payback (works), minimum call-out flag (works), CSV-like job parsing with error lines (works), usage opt-out (usage.mjs, 24 tests include it), robots/sitemap/JSON-LD/FAQ present. A code comment in calc.mjs says users can choose a 'custom' access factor but ACCESS has no custom entry and the parser rejects unknown access words, so that is a dead path (job.factor is never set by the UI). VENTURE.yaml stage is honestly 'prototype' with 'no cleaner has used it'. The 'route pack' is a day pack by job duration only: no geography or travel chaining between jobs.
evidence.verification: Test command run: 24 of 24 pass. Seeded three mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted with git checkout (git status clean afterwards): (a) dropped `overhead` from the total: caught (1 test failed, 'cost adds labour...'); (b) price = total/(1+margin) instead of (1-margin): caught (2 failed, margin test and curve test); (c) vehicle cost set to 0: caught (1 failed, cost test). Gaps: no test for margin clamp at 90%, no test of crew > 1 price end to end, no test of the access-factor numbers, dayPlan tests check capacity but not first-fit ordering or revenue values, and page.test.mjs only greps the HTML (the in-page glue in index.html has no behavioural test).
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script block. calc.mjs is small, pure, dependency-free and readable. Defects: marginPct is silently clamped to 0..90 with no message to the user (a 95% target quietly yields 90%); panels is not validated inside jobCost (0 panels gives perPanel Infinity, only parseJobs guards it); dead 'custom' factor branch (job.factor); the margin helper `money` rounds to whole dollars so a $0.50-per-panel difference is hidden in tables; Math.floor(opts.crew)||1 silently turns 0.5 crew into 1. Page tests assert absence of fetch/XHR, a good privacy guard. No linter or type check.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'nothing leaves the browser' is backed by page.test.mjs regex for fetch/XHR/beacon and local-only imports (true). Disclaimer text and sponsor link present (tested). 'Access factors are rough defaults' stated on page and README (honest). Problems: llms.txt links to https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/solar-panel-cleaning-quote-planner/, the retired Pages host, while VENTURE.yaml and README give https://marisstella.app/...; index.html canonical is `./index.html`, sitemap.xml `<loc>./index.html</loc>` and robots.txt `Sitemap: ./sitemap.xml` are relative URLs, which the sitemap protocol and robots.txt do not allow, so crawlers will ignore them. README says to run `node --test`, which Node 22 rejects in this repo. Page FAQ says the price curve shows 'the panel count at which your per-panel price covers fixed time', which the curve approximates but does not mark.
evidence.fitness: Walked a cleaner's job: enter rate, minutes/panel, setup, travel, margin, minimum charge, paste six example jobs, get price per job, per panel, day plan and annual plan; the customer payback block is usable at the door. Gaps a cleaner hits in the first hour: no default minutes-per-panel guidance or source, no way to save a price list (README admits it is next), no printable customer quote, no sales tax, no per-job travel chaining (each job pays full set-up and travel even when two are on the same street), no water/pure-water-system or per-visit equipment cost, no insurance or licence line other than the blanket overhead percent. Still, the core question 'what should I charge for 14 panels on a two-storey roof' is answered correctly from the user's own numbers.
evidence.domain: Compared with how cleaning businesses price (cost-plus on a target gross margin, a minimum call-out, per-panel rates above it): price = cost/(1-margin) is the right margin-on-price form, and the minimum-charge handling matches practice. Departures: access factors 1.0/1.15/1.4/1.9 and the 2 min/panel default are unsourced; the soiling-loss framing is the customer's guess, whereas published field studies (e.g. NREL soiling reviews) report typical annual soiling losses of a few percent in rainy climates and much more in dry or dusty ones, so the default 5% and the single yearly figure ignore rain-cleaning, tilt and seasonality (the page admits this in 'Not decided'); payback ignores that a clean recovers only part of the loss, panel degradation, and electricity-rate escalation. Working-at-height rules and insurance are explicitly out of scope, which a safety-minded reviewer would want flagged next to the 'double storey' factor rather than only in a footer.

defects.what: llms.txt points at the retired duncan-haywood.github.io Pages host instead of https://marisstella.app/solar-panel-cleaning-quote-planner/
canonical link, sitemap <loc> and robots Sitemap line are relative URLs, which crawlers ignore; the SEO files do not work as shipped
Target margin above 90% is silently clamped to 90% with no message, so the quote does not hit the margin the user typed
Day 'route pack' packs by duration only; every job pays full set-up and travel, so adjacent jobs overstate cost and price
Dead 'custom' access-factor branch and comment: ACCESS has no custom entry and parseJobs rejects it
README says `node --test`, which Node 22 rejects; should be `node --test '*.test.mjs'`
Tests miss the margin clamp, crew>1 end-to-end price and first-fit ordering; mutating the clamp or the packing order would pass

verdict: A small, honest prototype whose arithmetic is right: three independent hand recomputations (a single-person ground job priced $75.00, a two-person two-storey job priced $110.43, a payback of -$22 net with a 6.41% break-even) matched the code, 24 of 24 tests pass, and three of three seeded mutations were caught and reverted. It does not meet the bar because claims scores 2: llms.txt names a retired host and the canonical, sitemap and robots URLs are relative so the SEO files do not work. Domain and fitness are held at 2 by unsourced access factors and speed defaults, no per-visit travel chaining, a silent 90% margin clamp, and no saved price list or printable quote. Fixes are small (URLs, a margin warning, README command); the larger work is sourcing the access factors with a practising cleaner.
